question: Holi is popularly known as the festival of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Colors**__.

**__Key Points__**

• **Holi** is celebrated as the **Festival of Colors** because the central ritual involves people throwing and smearing each other with **Gulal** (colored powder) and colored water. This act symbolizes the arrival of **Spring** and the vibrant colors that bloom in nature during this season.

• The festival is observed on the **Purnima** (Full Moon day) of the **Hindu month** of **Phalguna**, which typically falls in **March** or late **February** in the **Gregorian calendar**.

• It signifies the **victory of good over evil**, commemorating the legend of **Prahlad** and **Holika**. **Prahlad** was a devotee of **Lord Vishnu**, while his father **Hiranyakashipu** and aunt **Holika** attempted to kill him. **Holika** was burnt to ashes in a fire while **Prahlad** remained unharmed, leading to the tradition of **Holika Dahan**.

• The festival is also deeply associated with the divine love of **Lord Krishna** and **Radha**. It is said that **Krishna**, who had a dark complexion, playfully applied color to **Radha** to match his own, starting the tradition of playing with colors in the **Braj** region of **Uttar Pradesh**.
